name: penthera
description: Offline cyber security agent for the user's own apps and AI coding tools, run locally with the Penthera CLI; open R&D, measured in public. Sets it up in one command ("set up penthera in this repo"). Scans the user's own live URL and repo (TLS, headers, auth, OpenAPI, secrets incl. AI keys, opt-in injection); checks npm and Python dependencies offline ("is this dependency safe?", "what changed in my deps?", "install X safely", "any AGPL in our deps?"); blocks secrets and risky agent config before commit ("add a pre-commit hook"); audits AI tooling ("audit my MCP servers / skills / hooks", "check this skill before I install it"); fixes findings on a local branch and re-scans to verify ("scan and fix my app"); writes reports and evidence ("report for my auditor / manager", NIS2, SARIF, baseline diff). Use when the user asks to scan, audit, harden, fix, or review the security of their own app, staging URL, localhost, repo, dependencies, or agent setup. Do NOT use for targets without explicit authorization.

All examples below use `penthera`; substitute `npx -y penthera@2.3.2` or `node bin/penthera.js` when needed.

To try a release candidate in someone's project, run it with `npx penthera@next ...` rather than `npm install penthera@next`. An install pins the exact rc in th
penthera --repo . -o reports/repo.json
If you run Penthera through `npx`, its hints print `npx penthera`. Run them as printed.

Offline and read-only: it reads `package-lock.json` and `node_modules`, or for Python `uv.lock` / `poetry.lock` / `pdm.lock` / `Pipfile.lock` / `requirements*.t
penthera deps                              # what every installed package can do
penthera install <pkg> --dry-run --json   # always start here: report only, nothing changes
penthera deps --license-policy permissive --json   # presets: permissive, weak-copyleft-ok, no-agpl
penthera init --dry-run --yes   # show the plan: detected items, checks, files it would write
penthera hook install   # .git/hooks/pre-commit; an existing hook is kept and runs first
2. If `core.hooksPath` is set (husky, lefthook), do not use `--force`; add `npx --no-install penthera hook run` to that tool's pre-commit config instead.
penthera ui --open                                   # this folder, reports in ./reports
- **Command injection:** never pass input to a shell. Use `execFile(cmd, [args])` with an allowlist; avoid `exec`/`shell=True`.
